title: Wastewater sampling and test procedures practice questions
description: Free practice questions on 40 CFR 136.1-136.3: approved test procedures, Table II preservation and holding times. Answers linked to the rule.

questions.question: Under 40 CFR 136.1(a)(3), the Part 136 procedures must be used for measurements required for which of these?

options.A: Laboratory proficiency tests a lab runs for its own customers
options.B: Certifications issued by States pursuant to section 401 of the Clean Water Act
options.C: Air emission permits issued under the Clean Air Act
options.D: Monitoring of drinking water at the consumer's tap

questions.explanation: Section 136.1(a)(3) lists "Certifications issued by States pursuant to section 401 of the Clean Water Act (CWA), as amended."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Besides Part 136 itself, which part of title 40 does 136.1(b) name for performing the measurements required for a sewage sludge permit application under section 405(f) of the Clean Water Act?

options.A: Part 141
options.C: Part 60
options.D: Part 503

questions.explanation: "The procedure prescribed herein and in part 503 of title 40 shall be used to perform the measurements required for an application submitted to the Administrator or to a State for a sewage sludge permit under section 405(f) of the Clean Water Act".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For the purposes of the NPDES program, what does 136.1(c) require when more than one test procedure is approved under Part 136 for a pollutant?

options.A: The test procedure must be sufficiently sensitive as defined at 40 CFR 122.21(e)(3) and 122.44(i)(1)(iv)
options.B: The permittee may use whichever approved procedure costs the least
options.C: The laboratory must run every approved procedure and report the average
options.D: The oldest approved procedure must be used

questions.explanation: "When more than one test procedure is approved under this part for the analysis of a pollutant or pollutant parameter, the test procedure must be sufficiently sensitive as defined at 40 CFR 122.21(e)(3) and 122.44(i)(1)(iv)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.1, Applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under the definition of detection limit in 136.2(f), the analyte concentration must be distinguishable from what?

options.A: The permit limit for the pollutant
options.C: The method blank results
options.D: The concentration in the upstream receiving water

questions.explanation: Detection limit is "the minimum concentration of an analyte (substance) that can be measured and reported with a 99% confidence that the analyte concentration is distinguishable from the method blank results".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 136.3(a), what controls when the reporting requirements of 40 CFR parts 122 and 125 conflict with reporting requirements associated with a listed method?

options.A: The method's own reporting requirements
options.C: The stricter of the two, as chosen by the analyst
options.D: The provisions of 40 CFR parts 122 and 125

questions.explanation: In that event, "the provisions of 40 CFR parts 122 and 125 are controlling and will determine a permittee's reporting requirements."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 136.3(c), when the Director establishes limitations on the discharge of a parameter for which there is no test procedure in Part 136 or in 40 CFR parts 405 through 499, who specifies the test procedure?

options.A: The Director
options.C: The manufacturer of the sampling equipment
options.D: The Alternate Test Procedure Program Coordinator

questions.explanation: "In these instances the test procedure shall be specified by the Director."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 136.3(d), upon whose recommendation may the Administrator approve additional alternate test procedures for nationwide use?

options.A: The State drinking water administrator
options.C: The Regional Administrator of the Region where the discharge occurs
options.D: The Alternate Test Procedure Program Coordinator, Washington, DC

questions.explanation: "The Administrator may approve additional alternate test procedures for nationwide use, upon recommendation by the Alternate Test Procedure Program Coordinator, Washington, DC."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Table II and limited use changes
questions.question: Under 136.3(e), how does the information in Table II rank against information in specific methods?

options.A: Specific methods always take precedence over Table II
options.B: Information in the table takes precedence over information in specific methods or elsewhere
options.C: Table II applies only when a method gives no holding time
options.D: The analyst chooses between them for each sample

questions.explanation: "Information in the table takes precedence over information in specific methods or elsewhere."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Table II and limited use changes
questions.question: Under 136.3(e), how may applications for limited use changes in preservation, containers or holding times for samples from a specific discharge be made?

options.A: By letters to the Regional Alternative Test Procedure (ATP) Program Coordinator or the permitting authority in the Region in which the discharge will occur
options.B: By a note in the laboratory's bench sheet, with no application needed
options.C: By publishing a notice in the Federal Register
options.D: By a phone call to the sampling equipment vendor

questions.explanation: "Applications for such limited use changes may be made by letters to the Regional Alternative Test Procedure (ATP) Program Coordinator or the permitting authority in the Region in which the discharge will occur."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Table II and limited use changes
questions.question: What time frame does 136.3(e) set for the decision on a request to deviate from the prescribed Table II requirements?

options.A: Within 10 days of receipt
options.C: Within 30 days of the first sample
options.D: Within 90 days of receipt of the application by the Regional Administrator

questions.explanation: A decision on such a request "will be made within 90 days of receipt of the application by the Regional Administrator."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: In footnote 1 to Table II, what does the container code "PA" mean?

options.A: Polyethylene only
options.C: Any plastic that is made of a sterilizable material (polypropylene or other autoclavable plastic)
options.D: Low density polyethylene

questions.explanation: Footnote 1 says "PA" is "any plastic that is made of a sterilizable material (polypropylene or other autoclavable plastic)", while "LDPE" is "low density polyethylene."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under footnote 2 to Table II, for a composite sample collected with an automated sampler, when must the sample be refrigerated at ≤6 °C, unless Table II or the method specifies otherwise?

options.A: Only after it arrives at the laboratory
options.C: Only if the holding time will exceed 48 hours
options.D: Only after the last aliquot is analyzed

questions.explanation: For such a composite sample, "refrigerate the sample at ≤6 °C during collection unless specified otherwise in this Table II or in the method(s)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under footnote 2 to Table II, if a composite measurement is required but a composite sample would compromise sample integrity, how are the individual grab samples collected at prescribed time intervals to be analyzed?

options.A: Only the last grab sample is analyzed
options.B: Only the grab sample with the highest reading is reported
options.C: They are poured together in the field without any check
options.D: Separately, with the concentrations averaged

questions.explanation: "Grab samples must be analyzed separately and the concentrations averaged." They may also be composited in the laboratory only "if the compositing procedure produces results equivalent to results produced by arithmetic averaging of results of analysis of individual grab samples."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under footnote 3 to Table II, when a sample is to be shipped by common carrier or sent via the U.S. Postal Service, who is responsible for ensuring compliance with the Department of Transportation Hazardous Materials Regulations?

options.A: The person offering such material for transportation
options.C: The Regional ATP Coordinator
options.D: The permitting authority

questions.explanation: "The person offering such material for transportation is responsible for ensuring such compliance."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under footnote 18 to Table II, to which samples does the preservation temperature not apply?

options.A: Samples shipped overnight
options.C: Samples that are analyzed immediately (less than 15 minutes)
options.D: Samples held in glass containers

questions.explanation: "The preservation temperature does not apply to samples that are analyzed immediately (less than 15 minutes)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: In Table II, what preservation does the row "47. Winkler" (listed after "46. Oxygen, Dissolved Probe") give?

options.A: Cool and add sulfuric acid
options.C: Fix on site and store in dark
options.D: Freeze at the laboratory

questions.explanation: The Winkler row lists containers "G, Bottle and top" and the preservation "Fix on site and store in dark"; the probe method row above it says "None required".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under footnote 4 to Table II, when does the holding time begin for a composite sample collected with an automated sampler?

options.A: At the time of the first aliquot
options.B: When the sample arrives at the laboratory
options.C: At the time of the end of collection of the composite sample
options.D: When the preservative is added

questions.explanation: For such a sample, "the holding time begins at the time of the end of collection of the composite sample." For a grab sample, "the holding time begins at the time of collection."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under footnote 4 to Table II, when does the holding time begin for a set of grab samples composited in the field or laboratory?

options.A: At the time of collection of the last grab sample in the set
options.B: At the time of collection of the first grab sample in the set
options.C: When compositing in the laboratory is finished
options.D: At midnight on the day of collection

questions.explanation: "For a set of grab samples composited in the field or laboratory, the holding time begins at the time of collection of the last grab sample in the set."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under footnote 4 to Table II, what two things are needed before samples may be held for longer periods than the times listed?

options.A: A signed chain-of-custody form and a cooler with ice
options.B: Data on file showing the analytes are stable for the longer time for the specific types of samples, and a variance from the Regional ATP Coordinator under 136.3(e)
options.C: Approval from the sampling equipment manufacturer and a second analyst
options.D: A written note from the plant operator and a duplicate sample

questions.explanation: Samples may be held longer "only if the permittee or monitoring laboratory have data on file to show that, for the specific types of samples under study, the analytes are stable for the longer time, and has received a variance from the Regional ATP Coordinator under § 136.3(e)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 136.3, Identification of test procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Footnote 23 to Table II extends the fecal coliform holding time for sewage sludge (biosolids) only, using EPA Method 1680 or 1681. Which sample types does it list?

options.A: All sewage sludge samples regardless of treatment
options.B: Class A composted, Class B aerobically digested, and Class B anaerobically digested
options.C: Raw influent and primary effluent
options.D: Final effluent samples from lagoons

questions.explanation: The extension covers "the following sample types using either EPA Method 1680 (LTB-EC) or 1681 (A-1): Class A composted, Class B aerobically digested, and Class B anaerobically digested."
